STEP 1 - Scene: A plate of roasted potato pieces (wedges/chunks with skin on, golden-brown edges). Photographed from directly above (top-down view).

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square-ish dinner plate, roughly 26 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (square plate, so slightly less, ~500 cm^2 usable).

STEP 3 - Items: Roasted potatoes (about 8-9 pieces, wedge-shaped, each roughly 4-5 cm long and 2-3 cm thick). No visible oil pool or sauce beyond light browning.

STEP 4 - Area: Potato pieces together cover roughly 30% of the plate (about 160 cm^2). Each piece is about 3-4% of the plate area; food covers roughly a third of the plate, not most of it.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pieces are fairly chunky, typical height ~2 cm for the pile envelope. 160 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 320 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Roasted potato chunks, cut vegetable density ~0.6-0.7 g/ml. 320 ml x 0.65 ≈ 210 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted potatoes with skin, cooked, about 110-120 kcal per 100 g (oil-roasted pieces run somewhat higher; use ~130 kcal/100 g to allow for a little oil absorbed). 210 g x 1.3 ≈ 273 kcal, round to ~270 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Eight to nine potato wedges covering about a third of a dinner plate at ~200 g is plausible. A few hundred kcal fits a side portion of roasted potatoes.

Totals: about 210 g, about 270 kcal.
